root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU invalidation path used unsigned address arithmetic that could overflow on `gather->end == ULONG_MAX`, causing the page-invalidation loop in `riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval()` to never terminate and the length check to miscompute due to `end - start + 1`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `unsigned long len = end - start + 1` and replaces `for (iova = start; iova < end; iova += PAGE_SIZE)` with a `do { ... } while (!check_add_overflow(iova, PAGE_SIZE, &iova) && iova < end);`, and changes the limit test from `len && len < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT` to `end - start < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT - 1`, explicitly noting it fixes overflow on the invalidation path for a sign-extended page table case.

intent_record.how: This change removes unused variables from the function. It does not alter runtime behavior, control flow, or IOTLB invalidation logic; it only eliminates dead local declarations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IOTLB invalidation range handling by using overflow-safe page iteration and a range-based threshold for per-page command emission.
intent_record.what: The page-by-page invalidation loop was changed from a `for (iova = start; iova < end; iova += PAGE_SIZE)` loop guarded by `if (len && len < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT)` to a `do { ... } while (!check_add_overflow(iova, PAGE_SIZE, &iova) && iova < end);` loop guarded by `if (end - start < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT - 1)`. A new local `unsigned long iova = start;` was introduced inside the branch, and the loop now uses `check_add_overflow()` when advancing `iova`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code still sends one invalidation command per page for small ranges, but the iteration is now overflow-safe when incrementing the address. The branch condition was also rewritten in terms of the address range length (`end - start`) rather than `len`, which changes when the per-page invalidation path is selected and avoids relying on the prior length check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval()`. It computes `unsigned long len = end - start + 1;` and then uses that value to choose whether to iterate per-page or send a whole-range invalidation: `if (len && len < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT) { for (iova = start; iova < end; iova += PAGE_SIZE) { ... } } else { ... }`. This is exactly the unsigned arithmetic pattern described in the root cause; if `end == ULONG_MAX`, `end - start + 1` can wrap, making `len` incorrect and potentially causing the page loop to misbehave. The loop condition `iova < end` also does not handle the inclusive `end` correctly and will not protect against overflow on `iova += PAGE_SIZE` when `start/end` are near `ULONG_MAX`. There is no guard or special handling for `ULONG_MAX`, so the fix is not present in this snippet.
